title: Session of First Presbyterian Church North Port v. The Presbytery of Southwest Florida
disposition_detail: Judgments: Issue 1 (whether Presbytery erred on September 8, 2012, by remanding the matter after declaring the Original CM Complaint administratively out of order) answered Yes; Issue 2 (whether Presbytery erred by directing and instructing the Session under BCO 40-4 apart from BCO 40-5 and 40-6 due process) answered Yes. The Complaint is sustained. Presbytery's instruction or direction to the FPC Session to initiate and prosecute formal process against CM was declared null and void because Presbytery failed to follow BCO 40-5.
first_summary: The SJC sustained the Session's complaint challenging Presbytery's handling of a member complaint. Presbytery wrongly remanded an untimely original complaint after declaring it out of order, and wrongly directed the Session to initiate formal process without following BCO 40-5. The complaint was sustained.
summary: The SJC sustained the Session's complaint against Presbytery. Presbytery had ruled a member's original complaint administratively out of order as untimely but then remanded the matter to the Session; the SJC held that once out of order, no complaint remained to remand. It also held Presbytery could not direct or instruct the Session to initiate formal process without BCO 40-5's required citation step, so those directions were null and void. The member remained under the Session's jurisdiction; the civil trespass order was not ecclesiastical discipline and did not alter membership.

evidence_notes.dispute: FPC Session challenged Presbytery's September 8, 2012 remand of an untimely member complaint and its actions directing or instructing the Session to initiate formal process against CM (lines 63–85, 91–93; printed pp. 568–570).
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: Issues 1 and 2 answered Yes; Complaint sustained (lines 95–99, 178). Reasons: the original complaint was untimely under BCO 43-2 and out of order, leaving nothing for Presbytery to remand (lines 135–161); BCO 40-5's first citation step was not followed before Presbytery supervised or directed the Session (lines 165–172); directions were null and void (line 178).
evidence_notes.qualifications: CM remained a member under the FPC Session's jurisdiction; the civil trespass order was not a judicial or ecclesiastical action and did not change her membership (lines 163, 174; printed pp. 572–573). No separate opinion text appears; only a concurrence/absence table is supplied (lines 182–184).

benchmark_examples: C01: preserve both successful and refused procedural claims; here both issues succeeded but the procedural posture is similarly central.
C02: distinguish legitimate investigation or supervision from formal censure; here BCO 40-5 supervision could not skip the required citation step.
